title: School zone speed limits review ordered
subtitle: Accessibility plan approved, Biehn Drive sewer and funeral home decisions deferred, Fergus Avenue approved, Bingeman Centre Drive speed review.
overview: Council directed staff to review speed limits and time-of-day restrictions in school zones on city streets, and the limits in all automated speed enforcement zones, with reports due before fall 2023. The motion was amended to cover all enforcement zones rather than only Westheights Drive and Franklin Street {{vote:m13}}. Council also asked staff to review whether Bingeman Centre Drive could move from 50 to 60 km/h.

Council approved the 2023-2027 Accessibility Plan, dismissed a development charges complaint for 375 New Dundee Road, and approved the planning applications for 142-146 Fergus Avenue and the Trussler West subdivision. Two items were put off until March 20: the Biehn Drive and sanitary trunk sewer environmental study report {{vote:m8}}, and the funeral home crematorium applications on Frederick and Becker Streets, deferred at the applicant's request.

The mayor reported that Regional Council's budget reinstated waste receptacles at Grand River Transit stops. Council also authorized the City Solicitor to settle an Ontario Land Tribunal appeal about Victoria Street South and Park Street properties, and moved the Audit Committee meeting from March 20 to April 17.

decisions.detail: Staff will investigate speed limits and time-of-day restrictions in city school zones and review limits in all automated speed enforcement zones, reporting back before fall 2023 {{vote:m13}}.
Council approved the 2023-2027 Accessibility Plan as the City of Kitchener's accessibility plan.

decisions.item: Development charges complaint, 375 New Dundee Road
decisions.detail: Council dismissed the complaint by McLean-Peister Limited about development charges imposed on its development.

decisions.item: Biehn Drive and sanitary trunk sewer environmental study
decisions.detail: Council deferred the study report to March 20 to review scoring of alternative 4, traffic needs, servicing options, flooding and salt concerns, housing supply impacts and Robert Ferrie Drive {{vote:m8}}.
Council adopted the Official Plan amendment, approved the zoning change and adopted the urban design brief for 142-146 Fergus Avenue.

decisions.item: Frederick and Becker Street funeral home crematorium
decisions.detail: Council deferred the Official Plan and zoning applications to March 20 at the applicant's request, to review parking, building design and Becker Street options.
Staff were directed to review whether the 50 km/h limit on Bingeman Centre Drive could increase to 60 km/h.
The City Solicitor was authorized to settle the tribunal appeal for 146-162 Victoria Street South and 92-110 Park Street, including signing Minutes of Settlement if needed.

debate: Supporters of the school zone review said consistency matters: 30 km/h applies at all hours on city streets, while regional roads use 40 km/h limited to school days and hours. One councillor said drivers should not be ticketed late on a Sunday night.

One councillor said residents in their ward found the 30 km/h limit hard to keep to and confusing. They cited changing limits along one route, vandalism of an enforcement camera, and reports of road rage.

One councillor supported the review cautiously, saying a school zone should be a school zone at any time of day and that time-based limits could weaken the purpose. The mayor noted staff's original advice was a consistent approach, since many school zones include year-round playgrounds and sports fields.

Staff said enforcement cameras make driver behaviour more noticeable, and cautioned against comparing regional arterial roads with lower-classification city streets. Staff expected to recommend keeping Bingeman Centre Drive at 50 km/h, describing it as a very wide road that is probably over-designed.

On Fergus Avenue, the applicant's consultant said adding one or two storeys would bring only a small number of affordable units, and the business case did not support the extra height. The seven-storey proposal stayed as is.
